title: bug: VS Code never reads daemon.json bindHost and dials 127.0.0.1 only, so for a live same-project daemon bound to ::1 or a LAN address every connect spawns a start the daemon refuses and fails naming nothing, and when another project's daemon holds the same port on 127.0.0.1 VS Code deletes the live daemon's daemon.json and starts a second daemon on the same .moe/ (VS Code twin of task-fe811130)
description:
Filed by hunt #19 (task-443e8eac), lane 1: the VS Code extension's daemon lifecycle. HEAD 3cd256eb.

JETBRAINS TWIN. task-fe811130 (DONE, f9395bf5) added MoeDaemonSupervisor.offLoopbackBindRefusal (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:965). It is used in ensureDaemonRunningImpl (:166) and in MoeProjectService.connect (MoeProjectService.kt:178). When a live same-project daemon is bound off loopback, JetBrains keeps daemon.json, starts nothing, publishes a status naming the host and schedules no reconnect. The loopback-serving set is LOOPBACK_SERVING_BIND_HOSTS (:1078): {127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::, wsl}, the daemon's probeHostFor set (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/probeHost.ts).

PROBLEM (moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts)
- Nothing under moe-vscode/src reads bindHost (0 grep hits). The daemon records it for every --host or MOE_BIND_HOST other than 127.0.0.1 (packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:848).
- Every dial uses moe.daemon.host, whose default is 127.0.0.1: getDaemonInfo :1563/:1588, ensureDaemonRunning :1664-1669, waitForDaemonInfo :1811.
- Live same-project daemon on ::1 or a LAN address, and nothing else on 127.0.0.1:<port>:
  - ensureDaemonRunning's TCP probe fails, so it spawns `start --project <path>` (:1669) on every connect.
  - The daemon's guard refuses that start: nocollide.sh shows exit 0 with daemon.json unchanged.
  - connect() then dials ws://127.0.0.1:<port>, which is ECONNREFUSED. The 5 s reconnect loop (maxReconnectAttempts 10, :777) repeats both steps, and no message names the bind host.
- Another project's daemon on 127.0.0.1:<port>:
  - The two binds can share a port, because the daemon's port check isLoopbackPortFree (index.ts:481, called from isPortAvailable :464) dials only 127.0.0.1. So a 127.0.0.1 daemon started after a ::1 or LAN-bound one takes the same number.
  - getVerifiedDaemonInfo's /health probe then reads 'foreign'. removeDaemonJsonIfUnchanged deletes the live daemon's daemon.json (:1542), and startDaemon('start') (:1543) starts a SECOND daemon on the same .moe/.

EVIDENCE (a snapshot of HEAD 3cd256eb outside the shared checkout; scripts and outputs are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-443e8eac/mine/)
1. zz-hunt443e-bindhost.test.cjs uses the tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs fixture with a stubbed spawn. daemon.json is {projectPath: <project>, bindHost: "::1", pid: <live>}, and a same-project daemon listens on [::1]:P. Output (bindhost-harness.out):
   no-collision: OBSERVED {"outcome":"rejected: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:33655","spawns":[["bundled-daemon.js","start","--project","<project>"]],"daemonJsonKept":true,"ownHealth":0,"ownWs":0,"messagesNamingBindHost":0}
   port-collision: OBSERVED {"outcome":"rejected: Moe could not find this workspace's daemon after refusing a foreign daemon.","spawns":[["bundled-daemon.js","start","--project","<project>"]],"daemonJsonKept":false,"ownHealth":0,"ownWs":0,"otherHealth":1,"messagesNamingBindHost":0}
2. zz-hunt443e-e2e.cjs uses real snapshot daemons:
   - A is `init --project A --host ::1 --port 19950`.
   - B is `init --project B --port 19950` and takes 127.0.0.1:19950 too.
   The real client, with a real spawn, then (bindhost-e2e.out):
   warning: "Moe: the daemon on 127.0.0.1:19950 serves .../projB, not this workspace (<A>). Starting this project's daemon on the next free port."
   A daemon.json now {"port":19960,"pid":2880254,"bindHost":null}
   health old A [::1]:19950 -> <A> (pid 2880002 alive: true)
   health new 127.0.0.1:19960 -> <A>
   That is two live writers on one .moe/.

FIX DIRECTION (JetBrains parity)
- Add an exported helper, offLoopbackBindRefusal(info, workspace). It returns a message when all of these hold, and null otherwise:
  - daemon.json's bindHost is a non-empty string outside {127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::, wsl};
  - the record names this workspace;
  - the record is from this side of WSL;
  - its pid is a positive integer that is alive (process.kill(pid, 0), as isPidAlive :1498).
- Only compare and show bindHost. Never dial, resolve or probe it: daemon.json is repository content. Put fixed words first, then the host.
- Run the helper in connect() before ensureDaemonRunning (:915). That makes it precede both the spawn and getVerifiedDaemonInfo's foreign removal.
- On a refusal: keep daemon.json, spawn nothing, show the message, and schedule no reconnect (manualDisconnect = true, as the protected refusal at :939 does).
- A configured moe.daemon.port endpoint keeps today's path.
- Out of scope: dialing bindHost. Also out of scope: a VS Code WSL-remote window facing a Windows-owned daemon, which is held back as a separate lead.

FILES: moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts; a new moe-vscode/tests/daemon-bindhost.test.cjs.

PLACEMENT: shares MoeDaemonClient.ts with task-e07e695c (the symlink row from this hunt). That row owns the four project-path comparisons (:184, :1576, :1656, :1861) and a helper beside pathsMatch. This row owns connect()'s new pre-check and its own helper. For "names this workspace", use task-e07e695c's helper if it has landed, or pathsMatch otherwise. There is no dependsOn.
definitionOfDone: With daemon.json {projectPath: <workspace>, bindHost: "::1", pid: <live>} and a same-project daemon on [::1]:P, connect() spawns nothing, leaves daemon.json byte-identical, schedules no reconnect and shows one message containing ::1. The same holds when 127.0.0.1:P answers /health as another project. A node --test file under moe-vscode/tests pins both and fails at 3cd256eb.

These keep today's path: bindHost absent, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, :: or wsl; a dead pid; a pid of 0 or less; a record from the other side of WSL. tests/daemon-identity.test.cjs and tests/daemon-start.test.cjs pass unchanged.
`cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` passes, run in a snapshot of the commit outside the shared checkout.

RED run in a whole-repo git-archive snapshot of HEAD 90c499e1 with only this file overlaid (node v24.21.0, npm ci ok): 8 fail, 5 pass. B1/B2/B3/B4 fail because connect() spawns `bundled-daemon.js start --project <project>` (deepEqual(f.spawns, []) gets one spawn): the refused `start` on every connect, as in hunt #19. B5 x4 (null matrix, message, EPERM pid, isOtherSideOfWsl) fail with 'offLoopbackBindRefusal / isOtherSideOfWsl is not a function'. The 5 B6 rows (configured port, configured host '[::1]', missing, unparseable and oversized daemon.json) pass at base by design: they guard today's path, so they cannot fail before the change. IPv6 loopback was available, so B1/B2 ran, not skipped.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT (DoD 1 and 2) in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, with the session's own editing tool. Mirror JetBrains' offLoopbackBindRefusal (task-fe811130, f9395bf5: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:965 and LOOPBACK_SERVING_BIND_HOSTS :1078). Do not edit JetBrains files.

1. Module scope, right after removeDaemonJsonIfUnchanged (:231-240), away from pathsMatch (:152), which task-e07e695c edits:
   - const LOOPBACK_SERVING_BIND_HOSTS = new Set(['127.0.0.1', '0.0.0.0', '::', 'wsl']). Comment it as the daemon's probeHostFor set (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/probeHost.ts) and JetBrains' twin.
   - const SHOWABLE_HOST = /^[0-9A-Za-z.:%_-]{1,255}$/. It allows no brackets, parentheses or spaces, because VS Code toasts render [text](link) markup (mem:gotcha-vscode-protected-refusal-ux).
   - export function isOtherSideOfWsl(projectPath: string, windows: boolean): boolean, with the JetBrains regexes: windows → /^\/(?![\\/])/; otherwise /^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]|[\\/]{2}[^\\/])/.
   - export function offLoopbackBindRefusal(record: unknown, workspace: string, windows: boolean): string | null. It returns a message only when all of these hold, and null otherwise:
     - isPlainObject(record) (:282);
     - bindHost is a string whose trim() is non-empty and outside the set;
     - projectPath is absent or '' (this workspace's own .moe/, as ensureDaemonRunning :1656 already treats it), or a string where pathsMatch(projectPath, workspace) holds. Use task-e07e695c's same-project helper instead if that row has landed;
     - a string projectPath is not isOtherSideOfWsl;
     - pid is an integer > 0 and alive.
   - Liveness: process.kill(pid, 0) means alive. An error whose errorCode (:275) is ESRCH means dead; any other error (EPERM) means alive, exactly as isPidAlive (:1498).
   - Error handling: the whole body is in try/catch returning null, so the helper never throws on malformed input.
   - Message: fixed words first, then the validated pid, then the host only when SHOWABLE_HOST matches, else 'an address other than 127.0.0.1'. For example: `Moe kept .moe/daemon.json and started no second daemon: this project's daemon (pid ${pid}) listens on ${shown}, but VS Code connects on 127.0.0.1 only. Stop that daemon, or restart it without --host or MOE_BIND_HOST, then reconnect.`
   - bindHost is compared and shown only. It is never dialed, resolved or probed, because daemon.json is repository content.
2. Add a private daemonBindRefusal(): string | null just before getVerifiedDaemonInfo (:1527). It returns null when:
   - moe.daemon.port > 0, or moe.daemon.host is not '127.0.0.1' (the user chose the endpoint);
   - there is no workspace;
   - daemon.json cannot be read or parsed: readDaemonJsonText plus JSON.parse in try/catch, so a missing, oversized or malformed file keeps today's path.
   Otherwise it returns offLoopbackBindRefusal(parsed, workspace, process.platform === 'win32').
3. connect(): call it synchronously right after `this.daemonShuttingDown = false;` and before `await this.ensureDaemonRunning();` (:913-915). On a refusal: this.manualDisconnect = true; log(refusal); vscode.window.showErrorMessage(refusal); throw new Error(refusal).
   - This mirrors the protected refusal at :937-941: no retry, JetBrains parity.
   - An explicit moe.connect or moe.reconnect re-runs the check, because connect() clears manualDisconnect at entry.
   - ensureDaemonRunning and getVerifiedDaemonInfo have no caller other than connect() (:915, :922).

Do not touch pathsMatch, comparableProjectPath, classifyIdentity, getDaemonInfo, ensureDaemonRunning or the STATE_SNAPSHOT handler: task-e07e695c owns those hunks. Then run the step-1 test file in the snapshot: every B row passes.
implementationPlan.note: MoeDaemonClient.ts: after removeDaemonJsonIfUnchanged I added LOOPBACK_SERVING_BIND_HOSTS, SHOWABLE_HOST, MAX_PID, exported isOtherSideOfWsl and exported offLoopbackBindRefusal(record, workspace, windows). I added a private daemonBindRefusal() before getVerifiedDaemonInfo. connect() calls it synchronously after `daemonShuttingDown = false` and before ensureDaemonRunning. On a refusal it sets manualDisconnect, logs, calls showErrorMessage and throws. pathsMatch, getDaemonInfo, ensureDaemonRunning, classifyIdentity and the STATE_SNAPSHOT handler are untouched. Two deviations from the plan text, both stricter. First, a pid above 2**31-1 reads as null: process.kill throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE for it, which would otherwise have counted as alive. Second, a non-string, non-null projectPath keeps today's path. I added the pid cases 2**31 and 1e300 and projectPath 42 to B5. GREEN in the scratch snapshot: daemon-bindhost 13/13, plus daemon-identity, daemon-start and protected-daemon-provenance unchanged, 123/123 pass, 0 skipped. Mutants M1-M5 on the scratch copy (no int32 cap, no other-side check, no manualDisconnect, no SHOWABLE check, ESRCH read as alive) each fail at least one B row. The full-suite gate is step 3.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the diff as an attacker who controls .moe/daemon.json, and as an unlucky user:

- Can any path still unlink daemon.json or spawn `start` for a live same-project off-loopback record (B2)? Check the reconnect timer, moe.reconnect and a connect() raced by disconnect().
- Do these behave exactly as before: a configured port or host, autoStart=false, a missing, unparseable or oversized daemon.json, a dead or reused pid, and a record from the other side of WSL?
- Is bindHost ever dialed, resolved or probed? It must not be.
- Does the diff stay out of task-e07e695c's hunks (pathsMatch, :184, :1576, :1656, :1861)?

If anything changes, re-run the step-3 command and use that fresh output for complete_task.
implementationPlan.note: Adversarial self-review of `git diff` (+62 in MoeDaemonClient.ts, plus the new test file). No edits, so the step-3 gate output still stands. (1) Repository text reaching a toast or log line: only the pid, shown after Number.isInteger, > 0 and <= 2**31-1, and bindHost, shown only when it matches SHOWABLE_HOST (no brackets, parentheses, slash or space, so no [text](link) and no URL). Otherwise the fixed phrase 'an address other than 127.0.0.1' is shown. projectPath is never shown. B4 asserts the toast, error and log lines hold no '](', 'command:' or 'reloadWindow'. (2) Other paths to unlink daemon.json or spawn `start` for a live same-project off-loopback record: ensureDaemonRunning and getVerifiedDaemonInfo are called only from connect() (grep). The check is synchronous and sits before both, so a disconnect() or dispose() cannot interleave. The refusal sets manualDisconnect, so scheduleReconnect returns early (B1-B4 assert reconnectTimeout stays undefined, state disconnected, connectInProgress false). extension.ts calls connect() only at activation, on moe.reconnect and on a settings path, and none of them watches daemon.json, so there is no loop. moe.connect or moe.reconnect clears manualDisconnect and asks again, which re-shows the one toast. (3) Today's path is kept for: a configured port or host; a missing, unparseable or oversized daemon.json; a dead pid; a pid <= 0, non-integer or over int32; another project's record; a record from the other side of WSL. B5 and B6 pin each. Deliberate choice: the pre-check also runs when moe.daemon.autoStart is false, because getVerifiedDaemonInfo's foreign-removal path deletes daemon.json and spawns `start` regardless of autoStart. Known trade-off: a reused pid makes a stale off-loopback record read as live, so VS Code keeps the record and asks for a restart (conservative, as in JetBrains). A bindHost such as 'localhost' or '127.0.0.2' is outside the loopback-serving set and is refused, as in JetBrains and per the contract. (4) bindHost is never dialed, resolved or probed: it is only compared with Set.has, tested with a regex and printed; probeDaemonIdentity and isPortOpen are not called by the new code. (5) The diff stays out of task-e07e695c's hunks: pathsMatch, classifyIdentity, getDaemonInfo, ensureDaemonRunning and waitForDaemonInfo are untouched. The three hunks are the module-level block after removeDaemonJsonIfUnchanged, the connect() pre-check, and daemonBindRefusal() before getVerifiedDaemonInfo. (6) Test file cleanup: every listener closes in t.after (ws clients terminated, closeAllConnections), every client is disconnected, every temp project is removed. The gate process exited on its own, so no handle was left open.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When .moe/daemon.json names this workspace's own live daemon (a positive integer pid that is alive, a record from this side of WSL, projectPath matching or absent) with a bindHost outside {127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0, ::, wsl}, and VS Code would dial its default 127.0.0.1 (moe.daemon.port unset and moe.daemon.host 127.0.0.1), connect() refuses before any startup work. It keeps daemon.json byte-identical, spawns no daemon, probes nothing, shows one error naming the host (only when it matches /^[0-9A-Za-z.:%_-]{1,255}$/, otherwise a fixed phrase) and schedules no reconnect. Every other daemon.json keeps today's connect path. This is VS Code parity with JetBrains' offLoopbackBindRefusal (task-fe811130).
acceptanceCriteria: A same-project live daemon.json with bindHost '::1': connect() spawns nothing, keeps daemon.json byte-identical, shows exactly one message containing ::1 and leaves no reconnect timer; the [::1] server sees no request.
The same record while another project's daemon answers on 127.0.0.1:<port>: no /health probe, no daemon.json removal, no spawn.

bindHost absent, '127.0.0.1', '0.0.0.0', '::' or 'wsl', a dead pid, a pid of 0 or less or non-integer, another project's record, a record from the other side of WSL, a missing, unparseable or oversized daemon.json, and a configured port or host all keep today's path.
A bindHost carrying link markup still refuses, but the message shows a fixed phrase instead of the text.
invariants: bindHost is never dialed, resolved or probed.
No repository text reaches a notification unless it matches SHOWABLE_HOST; projectPath is never shown; the pid is shown only as a validated positive integer.
The pre-check never throws on malformed input: any read, parse or liveness error keeps today's path.
pathsMatch, comparableProjectPath, classifyIdentity, getDaemonInfo, ensureDaemonRunning and the STATE_SNAPSHOT handler are unchanged (task-e07e695c owns them).
compatibility: A daemon.json written without bindHost (every 127.0.0.1 daemon) keeps today's connect path.
extension.ts's auto-connect .catch only logs (extension.ts:491-493), and moe.reconnect shows 'Failed to reconnect: <message>' as for any refusal.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) Dial bindHost when it names this machine, which is the daemon CLI's rule (decision-daemon-cli-bindhost-local-rule). Rejected: JetBrains' fe811130 twin never dials it, and dialing needs the CLI's isLocalAddress and IPv6-zone rules ported into the extension.
2) Guard only getVerifiedDaemonInfo's foreign removal. Rejected: it fixes the collision deletion but keeps the refused `start` spawn on every connect and the silent ECONNREFUSED loop.
3) Chosen: one synchronous pre-check at the top of connect(). It precedes ensureDaemonRunning's spawn, getVerifiedDaemonInfo's probe and removal, and every reconnect attempt, and the user-visible behavior matches JetBrains.
